`iptvGuideNowLetter`, 969–974) add 6 lines. **Total 2,520 lines.**

Terms:
- "Patch": one token edit in a retained activity declaration.
- "Temporary patch": a patch inside a declaration that a *later* phase moves. It becomes a moved-body
  substitution then.
- "Re-point": one edited forwarder in an existing controller property's Host object, i.e. a whole-property
  `patched` row (phase 5/8/9 precedent).
- "Substitution": one declared edit inside a moved body.

---

### 1. Summary and recommendation

**The user's sketch does not fit the budget.** The sketch is "phase 11 = core unit (+ `initIptvMode`) as a
multi-file set, phase 12 = EPG + VOD". The core unit is B9 = 2,067 lines, so phase 11 would be 72 % over
the ~1,200 budget. B9 must therefore be cut, without splitting the 6 shared fields.

The cut that respects that constraint has three parts:
- The **protocol core** goes first, with *all* 46 B9 fields in one owner. That owner is the single owner of
  `iptvUiContextToken`, `iptvBrowseToken`, `iptvZapRequestToken`, `iptvZapOwnsUiContext`,
  `iptvZapRequestInFlight` and `iptvZapPendingInputs`. Every writer of those 6 fields is in the owner's
  destination set, except `onDestroy`, which keeps 5 in-place patches, and `initIptvMode` (1 write), which
  stays retained.
- **Guide view-building code** (overlay builder, style, pickers, favourites/list membership, channel-jump
  dialog) goes second, together with EPG. This code reads and writes core state but owns none of the shared
  fields.
- **`initIptvMode` stays a retained, patched bootstrap.** It calls `bindViews`/`setupPlayer`/`setupSeekbar`/
  `setupControls`/`setupIptvControls`/`setupBackPressHandler`/`setupMetadataReceiver` and binds view fields
  for four owners. It is composition-root work.

| option | phase 11 | phase 12 | P11 patches (temporary) | P12 patches | re-points (P11 / P12) | P11 Host | P11 proofs | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R (recommended)**: core + VOD first | **1,250** (3 files) | **1,154** (3 files) | **134 in 24 decls (67 in 12 later-moving decls)** | 26 in 4 decls | 11 forwarders (12 token edits) in 2 props / 5 forwarders in 3 props | 23 members | 47 (2 new classifier forms) | fits budget; narrow Hosts; risk concentrated in P11 |
| R′: core without VOD | 1,138 | 1,266 | 123 (67) | 37 | 6 (in 2 props) / 10 (in 3 props) | 25 (+3 VOD forwarders) | 45 | P12 over budget; re-points the start-over Host twice |
| Reversed: overlay/pickers/EPG first | 1,154 | 1,250 | 32 (6) | 67 | 3 / 12 + **≈ 32 new temporary forwarders** | P11 Hosts ≈ 32 core forwarders + 13 | 20 | overlay writes core `iptvChannelAdapter`/`iptvSelectedCategory` through Host setters for a phase; wide Hosts (the phase-5 narrow-Host objection) |
| B (user sketch): full B9 + `initIptvMode` | 2,067 (5 files) | 453 (2 files) | 38 (6) | 13 | 4 forwarders (8 tokens) in 2 props / ≈ 25 forwarders | ≈ 60 (incl. 7 lifecycle setups, 15 EPG/header view setters) | 47 | fewest total edits, but 2,067 lines; documented exception only |

**Recommendation: option R.**

- **Phase 11, "IPTV guide protocol core"**: 1,250 moved lines, 92 members.
  - `TvIptvGuideController` (owner; all 48 fields + 14 guide/browse/search functions, ≈ 430 lines).
  - It eagerly constructs two fieldless nested collaborators: `TvIptvZapPager` (13 members, ≈ 525) and
    `TvIptvChannelNavigator` (zap keys, adjacent category, channel switch and VOD/episode navigation;
    17 members, ≈ 420).
  - One activity property at slot `iptvSeriesAudioKey` (838), and one 23-member Host shared by all three
    classes.
- **Phase 12, "IPTV guide chrome"**: 1,154 lines.
  - `TvIptvGuideChromeController` (owner; EPG pane + now/next header + 21 view/EPG fields, ≈ 400).
  - It eagerly constructs fieldless `TvIptvGuideOverlayBuilder` (overlay setup, style, source picker,
    channel-jump dialog, ≈ 475) and `TvIptvGuidePickers` (category/list pickers, favourites, row removal,
    ≈ 415).
  - One activity property at slot `iptvGuideCurrentName` (969), and one 13-member Host.

Phase 12 runs entirely on existing checker features (all 20 proofs are supported forms). Phase 11 needs two
narrow classifier forms (§2.3).

Why core-first beats the old phase-6 ordering (overlay+EPG first):
- **Hosts stay narrow.** The overlay builder reaches ≈ 28 core names and the pickers 11. Moving them first
  would mean ≈ 32 temporary forwarders into activity-retained core state, all re-pointed one phase later. It
  would also mean writing two core fields (`iptvChannelAdapter` from `setupIptvOverlay`,
  `iptvSelectedCategory` from the category picker) through Host setters.
- **Phase 12 then reaches all core state through one Host getter**, `host.iptvGuideController.` (phase-9
  `host.sourceSwitchController.` precedent).
- **The cost is the 67 temporary patches in phase 11.** They are mechanical `iptvGuideController[.pager|
  .navigator].` prefixes in 12 declarations that phase 12 moves, and they become 67 `host.iptvGuideController.`
  substitutions there.

The slot is the first removed field, `iptvSeriesAudioKey` (838). The activity property `iptvGuideController`

**All 47 later fields run earlier and each needs an exact inert proof** (checker forms per
`kotlin_move_partition.initializer_kind`):

| form | count | fields |
|---|---|---|
| constant `null`/`false`/`0`/int | 34 | every view ref, flag, token, `iptvZapPageSize` 200, `iptvZapMaxHiddenWindow` 600, … (`iptvPreferredAudioLang` included) |
| typed empty factory (supported) | 8 | `iptvBrowseChannels`, `iptvLists`, `iptvCategories`, `iptvZapCategories`, `iptvSearchSavedChannels`, `iptvSearchSavedCategories`, `iptvZapCachedChannels` (`mutableListOf<T>()`), `iptvZapCachedCategories` (`emptyList<String>()`) |
| **plain string literal, NOT supported** | 4 | `iptvSourceName = "IPTV"`, `iptvContentType = "live"`, `iptvZapSourceName = "IPTV"`, `iptvZapContentType = "live"` |
| **`java.util.ArrayDeque<Int>()`, NOT supported** | 1 | `iptvZapPendingInputs` |

**Step-T classifier extension, narrowly constrained.**
- A quoted literal with no `$`, no escapes and no newline → `constant`.
- Exactly `java.util.ArrayDeque<T>()` with explicit type arguments and no arguments → `allocation`.
- Negatives: `"$x"`, `"\n"`, `ArrayDeque(list)`, `ArrayDeque<Int>(n)`, an untyped `ArrayDeque()`.

Construction-order facts:
- No retained initializer between 838 and 1050 reads any moved field.
- Earlier-constructed controllers whose Hosts will forward into the owner are `iptvStartOverController`
  (798) and the existing Hosts. Their forwarders are computed and never read at construction. Add the
  existing "Host read during construction" fixture case for a forwarder into a later-slot controller.
- Nested `pager`/`navigator` construction is eager and fieldless. It is pinned structurally, with
  construction position inside the owner pinned.

#### 2.10 Hazards (each a step-T fixture/negative)

- **Shadowed locals.**
  - `val window` in `mergeIptvZapPage` (10523–10528, 5 uses; shadows `Activity.window`): must not become
    `activity.window`.
  - `val currentIndex` in `adjacentIptvCategory` (10622/10626; shadows the activity's `currentIndex`): must
    not become `host.`.
  - Parameter `title` in `refreshIptvBrowserChrome`/`requestIptvBrowse` (shadows `Activity.title`).
- **Receiver `this`:** `this.index` ×2 and implicit `index` (§2.6).
- **Default arguments.**
  - `requestIptvBrowse(action, query = iptvGuideSearch?.text?.toString()?.trim().orEmpty(), …)` reads owner
    state in the default, so it is evaluated in the callee at call time. Retained/temporary callers pass no
    `query` (8642, 8786, 8801, 9315 use defaults). Do not route the call through a Host.
  - Constant defaults on `switchToIptvChannel` (3 one-argument callers + the start-over Host explicit
    3-argument forwarder), `prefetchIptvZapPage(force)`, `requestIptvZapPage(anchor, fromEnd, onFailure)`,
    `refreshIptvBrowserChrome(title)`, `prefetch/requestAdjacentIptvCategory(attempt)`.
- **Two-level qualification:** `guide.pager.`/`guide.navigator.` in nested code, and
  `iptvGuideController.pager.`/`.navigator.` in activity patches and Host forwarders. Negatives: a missed
  hop, or a swapped pager/navigator target.
- **Overloads:** none among the 92 moved names. No Glide. 7 `Toast` sites (§2.6).
- **Templates:** no string template anywhere in the activity references a unit field, so there are 0 braced
  edits. Keep the negative.
- **Runnable self references:** none. Lambdas posted to the borrowed handler are not objects.
- **Order hazards.**
  - The owner is constructed at 838, before `iptvChannelStartController` (989) and the borrowed
    `iptvBrowseHandler` (1018).
  - The start-over controller (798) is constructed *before* the owner, but its re-pointed forwarders are
    computed.
  - Fixture: a construction-time read of a re-pointed forwarder must fail.
- **Smart-cast stability:** Host `val`s are interface getters (unstable). The moved code uses no smart cast
  on host vals (all used Host vals are non-null types or `?.`-chained). Confirmed by inspection; compile
  proves it.

### 4. `initIptvMode` decision

Keep it **retained**: 116 lines, patched 33 times in P11 and 16 times in P12.

Moving it would need a Host with 7 lifecycle-setup forwarders (`bindViews`, `setupPlayer`, `setupSeekbar`,
`setupControls`, `setupIptvControls`, `setupBackPressHandler`, `setupMetadataReceiver`), plus
`StremioSubtitleService(this)` (8292) and the `seekFeedbackManager`/`stremioSubtitleService`/
`iptvDecoderMode`/`isIptvMode` writes. It also has an unbraced `$currentIptvIndex` template at 8264 that
would need bracing if moved. It is bootstrap/composition-root code.

Recorded in the activity's end-state exception, next to `bindViews`/`parsePayload`. Revisit when the
playback-start phase moves `onCreate`'s helpers.

The original has two: `restoreIptvZapBootstrapFallback` line 9971

Activity `this` to the constructor before entering the receiver lambda. There
is no explicit `this` inside that lambda. Original bytecode pins
`invokespecial android/widget/EditText.<init>:(Landroid/content/Context;)V` at
line 10001. This dialog stays in the activity. Treating its constructor
argument as a receiver-lambda exclusion would be a false classification.
The draft checker rejects that classification, inventories the two actual
entry receivers, and pins their original contexts. Evidence:
`p11/receiver-design-finding.json`, `p11/original-psi.json` and the compiled
production fixture/audit. The inventory's implicit `entry.apply { index = 0 }`
remains entry-owned and is covered by a separate negative.

## Phase 11 step 0 — original IPTV core characterization (`00c60870e`)

The real `onCreate` IPTV bootstrap constructs Media3, binds the production
guide and installs its actual row, editor, scroll, navigation and numeric-dialog
callbacks. The fixture immediately releases that borrowed real player and uses
the existing observation proxy and binary fake Flutter messenger. Live and VOD
launches are separate; no device, emulator or network reply is involved.

All **134 new tests pass on the original**. They cover installed series/episode/live
selection, submit-only search and call-time default arguments, saved category
restoration, forward/backward scroll thresholds, guide animations and deferred
trim, page payloads and window identity/merge/bounds, pending-input FIFO and
reentrancy, adjacent category/cache behavior, numeric lookup and its installed
submissions, outgoing VOD checkpoints, Start Over retirement, startup-channel
memory, episode navigation/audio persistence, and the real remote-key matrix.

For page and browse replies, success/error/notImplemented each run inline and
queued on the main looper with request-token, UI-token and ownership changes
varied independently. An old page request preserves the newer in-flight flag;
a matching page with stale context or lost ownership clears its flag before
rejecting callbacks, queue clearing and Toasts. Jump replies deliberately check
only the request token. Separate cleanup-order mutations pin the difference.

The borrowed-handler cases pin deferred hide trimming and the exact 60-second
archive retry through the installed adapter EPG callback. Teardown observes all
three core token increments, flag/queue cleanup, callback rejection and borrowed
post cancellation, including cleanup before player release. The checker retains
the exact in-place statement order; no teardown is folded into a controller.

Fixture details: `ShadowActivity` has a separate focus slot, so the key helper
mirrors the actually attached window's focus before calling production
`dispatchKeyEvent`. Bootstrap EPG replies are completed with fresh archive
metadata to retire their 45-second watchdogs. The archive retry deadline is
measured from the original post's virtual uptime, accounting for UI frame work.
No production timing or lifecycle seam was added.

**Original-code mutation evidence:** every new named test has an assertion-failing
proof; **162 isolated mutations** are killed on detached `00c60870e` plus these
tests. Additional proofs cover cleanup-before-guard order, all token invalidations,
both scroll thresholds, duration literals, normalized input direction and all
five core teardown statements. Retained caller-wiring mutations remove row
selection calls, scroll/window routing, editor predicates, numeric submission,
physical-key dispatch and the VOD Next-button call. Compilation errors, crashes,
zero-test runs and assertion failures in unrelated tests are not accepted.

An initial scroll-boundary run reached an empty request accessor instead of an
assertion. It was rejected and archived in `p11/mutations-discarded/`; an
explicit request-emission assertion now rejects that unchanged mutant on an
assertion. The numeric error assertion is null-safe. Final fixture assertions
also observe cleanup before release and the paging/focus gates. No rejected run
is included in the 162 accepted proofs.

Raw definitions, patches, Gradle output, named-test XML and fixture hashes are
under `p11/mutations/`; `p11/mutations.json` and `p11/run_mutations.py` reproduce
the runs. Complete original characterization is archived in
`p11/characterization/` (134/134), and reverified after final fixture strengthening.
The detached original tree is removed after all evidence is recorded.

## Phase 11 step 0b — systematic IPTV core sweep (`00c60870e`)

Claude's first independent sample killed 8 of 18 original mutants. All ten
survivors are now assertion-killed, with the **exact first-occurrence mutation
strings** rerun against **all 230 phase-11 characterization cases** (134 prior
plus 96 additions). The complete final cohort also passes on the unchanged
original. No compile failure, crash or zero-test run is an accepted proof.

The new assertions pin null-page queue cleanup **before** the failure callback,
both source-name owners in jump/page replies, absent page and jump totals,
browse's zap-generation invalidation, selected-category preservation, and
execution-time guide visibility before search refocus. They also pin false
checkpoint suppression, live-only banner feedback, single-loaded-row paging
through real channel keys, and in-window adjacent prefetch. Inline and queued
reply cases retain the asymmetric token/ownership semantics from Step 0.

The broader sweep seeds distinct pre-existing state to make writes observable;
checks real adapter notifications, displayed titles/counts, GONE versus INVISIBLE,
attached-row focus and scroll; and records request payloads, callbacks, player
operations, Toasts, logs and selector parameters. It covers all source/content
arms, window identity/order/copying, guards, empty/wrong-type defaults, both
12-row prefetch edges, FIFO/reentrant drains, every cache field and invalidation,
category recursion/attempt bounds, channel-adoption branches and episode/live
controls. Explicit cases cover same-category cache clearing (otherwise masked
by installation), neighbour-preserving fallback, search retirement during a
page-only zap, duplicate categories at attempt exhaustion, mixed live/VOD
current-row reads, absent search-view defaults, and the exact 60-character
playback-log URL prefix. Every prior characterization assertion remains.

There are **96 isolated named assertion proofs**, one for each new test, plus
**541 distinct systematic original-code mutants (542 accepted proof runs)**
across every moved function.
Five named proofs were repeated after their final assertions were strengthened.
The ten exact Claude survivors were initially proved in isolation and then
rerun with the complete final cohort. Rejected discovery variants, including
compile-invalid deletions and cases masked by equal initial values or the wrong
cohort, remain under `p11/step0b/discovery-attempts/`; none are counted as kills.

Durable evidence: `p11/step0b/final-control-v3/` (230/230 original control),
`named-proofs/` and `named-proof-definitions.json` (96 single-test proofs),
`sweep/` and `sweep.json` (542 accepted runs, 541 distinct mutants), and
`claude-survivors-final/` (exact ten mutations, 230 cases per run). Each includes
raw patches, Gradle output, XML and fixture hashes; the runners restore original
production bytes in `finally`. Earlier controls/refinements are preserved.
The detached original evidence worktree is removed after verification.

### Per-function coverage matrix

The offline Kotlin 2.2.20 PSI collector inventories **800 original sites** within
the exact manifest spans: **199 writes, 105 if conditions, 416 calls, 77 returns,
two when expressions and one loop**, across all **44 moved functions**. The five
same-name retained Host-forwarder hits outside those spans are excluded.
`p11/step0b/moved-obligations.json` records each original source span/line;
`coverage-matrix.json` maps every site to named assertions and accepted proofs.
Nested pure calls are grouped with their value/condition/output assertions;
terminal returns are checked through the corresponding guards and outcomes.
They are not claimed as 800 independent mutation runs. Direct state writes,
posts, side effects and conditions have their own mutation witnesses; extra
value mutations pin copying, ordering, endpoint selection, defaults and bounds.
The table below lists every function, all site counts and its asserted outcomes;
raw node-level IDs, exact assertions and proof relationships are in the JSON.

W/C/I/R/X mean write / call / if / return / when-or-loop site counts. Proof ranges
are shown compactly; the mutation table and raw definitions enumerate them.

## Phase 12 step 0b — URL, deferred-current and input boundaries

Ten additional original-surface cases pass on `b870a16b1`; every case has a
named assertion mutation proof. Claude's exact o03/o06/o12 replacements were
re-run separately against **all 163 phase-12 tests**, with a 163/163 passing
control and matched 1 GiB worker heap: all three are assertion-killed. Complete
logs, XML, definitions, fixture hashes and accepted proof records are under
`p12/step0b/`. The initial two zero-input probes failed in the test's unsafe
nullable error conversion; those crash-only variants are rejected and archived
under `preliminary-null-error-proofs/`. The final null-safe assertions fail as
assertions, with no production change.

### 3. Phase 13 feasibility record: playlist overlay + focus navigator + guide skin

### 3.1 Summary and recommendation

**Selected:**
- `TvPlaylistOverlayController` (owner, ≈ 575 lines);
- nested `TvPlaylistFocusNavigator` (≈ 325), which owns the focus-engine state (variant B);
- nested `TvPlaylistGuideSkin` (≈ 395), which owns the skin views and flags.

Both nested classes are constructed eagerly inside the owner's initializer, following the phase-6/8/11
precedent. There is one 11-member Host, shared, plus the injected `AppCompatActivity`. The activity
property sits at the first owned slot, `seasonTabs` (182).

| item | count |
|---|---|
| moved members / lines | **60 / 1,199** (24 properties, 36 functions) |
| activity patches | **31 in 15 declarations**, of which 18 sit in later-moving code (ROUTERS 5, START 6, CTRL 2, SHUF 7) |
| Host re-points | **7 forwarders in 6 properties** (whole-property `patched` rows) |
| Host | 11 members; ≈ 115 `host.` substitutions |
| initializer proofs | **28** (3 new narrow classifier forms; §3.3) |
| receiver substitutions | 8 `this` → `activity` (2 `Glide.with`, 2 `TextView`, 2 `LinearLayoutManager`, 1 `GridLayoutManager`, 1 `ContextCompat`); 1 excluded object self-receiver |
| inherited-receiver audit | 15 (14 `findViewById`, 1 `layoutInflater`) |
| cross-file qualifications | **49** (variant B; compile-checked) |
| visibility substitutions | ≈ 33 |
| substitutions total | ≈ 220 |
| reflective retargets | 10 literal sites through **4 owner-map routes**; 0 public-function pins |
| Dart retargets | 0; one anchored `_between` range gets 4 patches, and its assertions are unaffected |
| lifecycle | 7 in-place `onDestroy` patches; no `onStart`/`onStop`/`onPause`/`finish` edits |

**Risk: medium-low.** It is deterministic view code, with no Flutter token protocol, no coroutine, and no
player-thread state. The risks are:
- DPAD focus timing: a handler post at 100 ms, `View.postDelayed` at 50/100 ms, a self-removing global-layout
  listener, and focus-recovery attach/detach callbacks;
- skin-specific axis remapping;
- a session-fixed `controlsSkin` lazy.

**Test gap: high.** No existing test drives the overlay wiring, the focus engine or the guide skin. Phase 1
covered only `PlaylistAdapter`/`MoviePlaylistAdapter` binding.

**Why it beats the alternatives:**
- SUBF (1,113 lines / 36 patches) has a similar ratio, but it has 45 reflective sites and an async fetch
  and search protocol.
- TUNE has the worst test gap.
- The controls units need Hosts of 80–87.

There is one slot: the owner's property replaces `seasonTabs` at 182, between `skipSegmentButton` (181)
and the seekbar views (186). Both nested classes map to that slot. **Every moved property other than
`seasonTabs` runs earlier, so there are 28 proofs:**

| fields | form | kind |
|---|---|---|
| `movieTabs = mutableListOf<MovieTab>()` | typed empty factory | allocation |
| `playlistVisible = false`, `isNavigating = false`, `guideSkinInstalled = false` | literal | constant |
| `playlistAdapter`/`seriesPlaylistAdapter`/`moviePlaylistAdapter`/`movieGroups`/`focusRecoveryRunnable` `= null`; 13 × `gd* = null` | literal | constant |
| `guideGridSpan = 5` | literal | constant |
| `focusRecoveryHandler = Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())` | handler | handler-allocation |
| **`playlistMode: PlaylistMode = PlaylistMode.NONE`** | **new: enum entry** | constant |
| **`navigationTargetPosition = -1`** | **new: negative integer literal** | constant |
| **`guideOverlayLayoutRes` / `guideItemLayoutRes`** (`get()` only, no backing field) | **new: accessor-only, no initializer** | none-run |

**Step-T classifier additions** (narrow, each with negatives):
- **Unary-minus integer literal.** The current regex accepts only `[0-9]…`.
  - Accept `-` followed by the existing constant form only. Reject `-x` and `-f()`.
- **Enum entry of a reviewed enum.** Accept `PlaylistMode.NONE` from an explicit allow-list (`PlaylistMode`
  is `internal enum class PlaylistMode { NONE, SERIES, COLLECTION }` in `TvPlaybackPayload.kt`, with no
  `init` or constructor). Its first access triggers only that enum's static initialization.
  - Reject non-listed types.
  - Reject `X.y()` calls and companion/property reads.
- **Accessor-only property.** Prove from the PSI that there is no initializer and no delegate, and only a
  getter. Nothing runs at construction, so classify as `none`.
  - Reject `by lazy`.
  - Reject a backing initializer plus a getter.

No `lateinit` property moves.

- There is no borrowed `progressHandler`/`controlsHandler`, no coroutine, and no `MethodChannel` (the only
  async edge is `sourceFetchController.requestEpisodeFetch`).
- Teardown order is unchanged (§3.4).

  This is existing; no change.

  fallback). Pin it.

Production remains byte-identical to the phase-12 merge. **120 new tests** use real `onCreate`/`start`/`resume`/visible activity bootstrap, seven independently instantiated controls skins, real adapter/key/focus/click callbacks, typed reflection and paused-looper delivery. The workers and clean baseline use the same evidence-only 1 GiB heap; repository Gradle settings are unchanged.

Coverage includes exact seven-skin layout/item getter pairs, replacement child counts, 13 nullable bindings, font/geometry/color states, detail/chrome strings and artwork lifecycle; series/movie filtering and real callback wiring; default scroll/force dispatch and refresh notifications; header skipping, pending targets, off-screen scroll requests, focused-child precedence, 50/100 ms delivery, retry ordering, cancellation/replacement and evaluation-time guards. The original unconditional older reset, queued View work after hide/rebuild/destroy and accumulating global focus listeners are deliberately pinned. Compiled teardown order and actual cleanup before the finished message cover all seven phase-13 statements.

### Mutation evidence

Every new test has its own named assertion-failing proof on the original (`named-proof-definitions.json`, `named-proofs/results.json`). Shared mutants are compiled once, but each listed JUnit identity must independently fail on its assertion. Additional statement, callback, diagnostic, branch, list-write and year-boundary mutations strengthen the net. A compiler error or crash is never credited as a kill; type-safe replacements preserve smart casts. Filtered survivors are rechecked against the entire phase-13 set, with stronger preconditions/output assertions where required.

| Batch | Runs | Assertion kills | Evidence |

| repairs | 24 | 22 | `p13/step0/repairs/results.json` |

The following six deletions are equivalent on the production inputs; compatibility code remains intact. Prefetch and NO_POSITION assignments also have assertion-failing value perturbations.

| Node / deletion | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `o379` / `write-o379` | Fresh unattached TextView: the immediately following setFocusableInTouchMode(true) sets both FOCUSABLE_IN_TOUCH_MODE and FOCUSABLE. There is no intervening observer or parent. Deleting the preceding isFocusable=true assignment leaves the observable flags unchanged. |
| `o562` / `write-o562` | Fresh unattached TextView: the immediately following setFocusableInTouchMode(true) sets both FOCUSABLE_IN_TOUCH_MODE and FOCUSABLE. There is no intervening observer or parent. Deleting the preceding isFocusable=true assignment leaves the observable flags unchanged. |
| `o266` / `write-o266` | The newly constructed LinearLayoutManager already defaults isItemPrefetchEnabled to true. Deletion is equivalent; replacing the value with false is killed by the bootstrap property assertion. |
| `o524` / `write-o524` | At the NO_POSITION branch, a nonnegative navigationTargetPosition would itself have been selected as currentPosition. Production writes only -1 or nonnegative targets, so this branch already has target=-1. Deletion is equivalent on reachable states; assigning 0 is killed by the missing-position assertion. |
| `o694` / `effect-o694` | On stable nonempty input, main is never empty: when maxSize<=0 the small-file predicate is false; otherwise at least one maximum-size item is >= the 40% threshold (including a threshold rounded to zero). The main.isEmpty rescue branch is unreachable through the real synchronous UI callers. Deleting main.addAll(extras) there is equivalent. The guard inversion is killed; compatibility code remains untouched. |
| `o695` / `call-o695` | On stable nonempty input, main is never empty: when maxSize<=0 the small-file predicate is false; otherwise at least one maximum-size item is >= the 40% threshold (including a threshold rounded to zero). The main.isEmpty rescue branch is unreachable through the real synchronous UI callers. Deleting extras.clear() there is equivalent. The guard inversion is killed; compatibility code remains untouched. |

Android SDK 28 `View` and RecyclerView constructor bytecode/provenance are archived beside the results. The unreachable Main/Extras rescue is retained, and its guard inversion fails an assertion. Discarded frame/cohort experiments are excluded from the accepted totals.

## Phase 14 inventory (at `315448a3c`; re-measure on `82b16832c`)


Source: `android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/debrify/app/tv/AndroidTvTorrentPlayerActivity.kt` at
`315448a3c` (phase-12 merge, **10,297 lines**, class header 136, 559 depth-1 members). This is a read-only
survey of the main checkout. Nothing was built and nothing under `../debrify-wt/` was touched.

**Tooling.** The p13 scripts were copied to `scratchpad/p14/` and re-indexed on the current file:
- `idx.py`: a brace/string/comment-aware member indexer;
- `refs.py` / `unit.py`: word-boundary reference scans. They count templates and `this@Activity.`, and
  exclude other receivers;
- `subf.py` / `split.py`: unit membership and cross-file counts;
- `refl.py`: quoted reflective names in `android/app/src/test`.

Every count below was checked by hand against the source. Terms are as in the phase-11/13 inventories:
- **patch**: a token edit in a retained activity declaration;
- **re-point**: an edited forwarder in an existing controller property's Host object, which makes that
  property a whole-property `patched` row;
- **substitution**: a declared edit inside a moved body.

**Phase 13** (playlist overlay + focus navigator + guide skin, in progress elsewhere) is treated as a
controller. Scanned interplay: **0 references in either direction** between SUBF and the phase-13 unit.
Both phases patch different statements in five shared declarations: `playbackListener`, `onCreate`,
`handleMetadataUpdate`, `playMediaDirect`/`playPikPakVideoWithRetry`, and `onDestroy`. Re-measure on the
phase-13 merge and merge the manifests. All spans after ≈ 182 shift by the phase-13 removals (≈ −1,180
in total, mostly before the SUBF function spans).

### 1. Summary and recommendation

**Do not merge into `TvSubtitleController`. Use a sibling owner plus one fieldless collaborator.** There
are three reasons:
1. **Size.** `TvSubtitleController.kt` is already **776** lines. Adding 1,094 moved lines gives ≈ 1,870;
   adding only the fetch block (430) still gives ≈ 1,230. Both are over the 800-line limit.
2. **Frozen destination.** Every earlier destination, including the phase-4 file, is frozen byte-identical.
   A merge needs an earlier-destination exception, which no phase has used.
3. **Self-forwarders.** The phase-4 Host has 9 forwarders into this unit. After a merge they would become
   self-references inside the phase-4 file, which are non-verbatim edits.

The responsibilities also differ:
- The phase-4 controller owns **rendering, track selection, the settings panel and the
  timing/appearance/embedded menu rows**.
- SUBF owns the **external subtitle sources**: addon fan-out and fetch, injected captions, the manual
  identity, auto-selection, the catalog search and its dialogs, and the subtitle menu column/addon/search
  rows.

**Selected (variant B′, ≈ 1,094 lines, 43 members):**
- **`TvSubtitleSourcesController.kt`** (owner, **642 member lines → ≈ 712 lines**). It holds all 21 moved
  fields and 17 functions: reset, fetch fan-out, auto-select, manual identity, identity label and the 4 UM
  subtitle row builders. The activity property `subtitleSourcesController` sits at the `stremioSubtitles`
  slot (1261), with `@OptIn(UnstableApi::class)` at class level (as in `TvSubtitleController`; it uses
  `HlsManifest` and Media3 `Format` fields).
- **`TvSubtitleSearchDialogs.kt`** (fieldless, **452 member lines → ≈ 487 lines**). It holds 5 functions:
  `showSearchSubtitleDialog`, `getCurrentSubtitleSearchItem`, `requestSubtitleCatalogSearchFromFlutter`,
  `createSubtitleCatalogResultAdapter` and `showSeasonEpisodePrompt`. The owner constructs it eagerly as
  `val dialogs = TvSubtitleSearchDialogs(activity, host, this)` (the phase-11/12/13 precedent). It reaches
  owner state only as `sources.x`.
- **One shared 15-member Host**, all members computed and explicitly qualified. No Host `var` is needed:
  moved code never writes an activity field.

| item | count |
|---|---|
| moved members / lines | **43 / 1,094** (21 fields, 22 functions) |
| activity patches | **24 in 9 declarations** (§4.1) |
| Host re-points | **12 forwarders, 14 token edits, in 4 controller properties** (§4.2) |
| initializer proofs | **20** (1 new classifier form: `emptyList()`; it reuses the phase-13 `-1` form) |
| cross-file qualifications | **10** (owner→dialogs 5, dialogs→owner 5; no cross-file write) |
| Host substitutions | **77** (owner 46, dialogs 31) |
| receivers `this`→`activity` | **22** (owner 4 incl. 1 `this@Activity`, dialogs 18); 1 excluded receiver |
| inherited-receiver pins | **3** (`runOnUiThread`) plus **6 reviewed non-substitution pins** (`context` ×4, `getItem`, named arg `resources =`) |
| visibility substitutions | **22** (owner 18, dialogs 4; public, never `internal fun`) |
| substitutions total | **≈ 134** |
| reflective retargets | **34 literal sites, 7 names, 5 files → 7 owner-map routes**; 0 function pins (rescan after step 0) |
| Dart retargets | **0**. One anchored range (`handleMetadataUpdate`) gets 1 patch; its asserted literals are untouched |
| lifecycle | **1 in-place `onDestroy` patch**; no `onStart`/`onStop`/`onPause`/`finish` edits |

**Activity:** ≈ −1,094 + ≈ 22 (property + Host) = **≈ −1,072**. That is ≈ 9,140 → **≈ 8,070** after phase 13.

**Risk: medium-high.** The test gap is **high**. No JVM test drives addon fetch, injected captions, manual
identity, catalog search, either dialog or the UM subtitle column. Only the pure policies
(`chooseAutomaticSubtitle`, `SubtitleTrackReadiness`, `SubtitleSearchQuery` helpers) and the phase-4
rendering paths (through the Host fields) are covered. The specific risks are:
- two async protocols (per-addon slot tokens + content token; Flutter metadata and catalog-search
  replies);
- coroutines on the borrowed `subtitleScope`;
- two `AlertDialog`s built from code;
- bidirectional coupling with the phase-4 controller (18 `host.subtitleController.` reads; 9 re-pointed
  phase-4 forwarders).

**Reconciliation with the phase-13 plan's estimate.** The plan said "45 / 1,113, 36 patches (11), ≈ 14
re-points in 6, 45 reflective sites". The differences:
- **Members and lines.** Re-measured at `315448a3c`, there are 44 members / 1,095 lines. Keeping
  `subtitleTrackReadiness` in the activity gives 43 / 1,094.
- **Patches.** That scan counted 2 `return@requestSubtitleCatalogSearchFromFlutter` label tokens, which are
  not patches. It also counted the 7 `subtitleTrackReadiness` sites, which do not move under this
  recommendation.
- **Re-points.** The 2 `subtitleTrackReadiness` re-points also disappear.
- **Reflective sites.** The 45 were 36 quoted moved names plus the 9 `subtitleScope` sites, which stay
  borrowed. Of the 36, the 2 `resetSubtitleState` sites in `NativePlayerSettingsConsumptionTest` reflect
  **`TorboxTvPlayerActivity`** (Java, its own private method), so they are unaffected. That leaves 34 real
  retargets.

| form | fields | count | classifier |
|---|---|---|---|
| typed empty factory | `addonSubtitleResults`, `injectedSubtitles`, `addonFetchTokens`, `failedSubtitleUrls` | 4 | existing (p5) |
| boolean literal | `suppressSubtitleAutoSelect`, `subtitleAddonDiscoveryReady`, `isLoadingStremioSubtitles`, `userManuallySelectedSubtitle` | 4 | existing |
| `0` / `1` | `addonSubtitleFetchToken`; `pendingSeason`, `pendingEpisode` | 3 | existing |
| `null` | `manualSubtitle*` ×5, `pendingSeriesResult` | 6 | existing |
| `-1` | `currentStremioSubtitleIndex` | 1 | **phase-13 unary-minus form** (add it here if phase 13 did not land it) |
| string literal `""` | `subtitleSearchStatus` | 1 | existing (p11) |
| **`emptyList()`** (no type arguments; the type comes from the declaration `List<SubtitleCatalogResult>`) | `subtitleSearchResults` | 1 | **NEW** |

**Classifier rules for `emptyList()`.**
- **Accept:** the no-argument stdlib `kotlin.collections.emptyList` with an explicit declared property
  type. It returns the `EmptyList` singleton, so there is no allocation and no state read.
- **Negatives:**
  - `listOf()` / `listOf(x)`;
  - `emptyList().toMutableList()` or any chained call;
  - an `emptyList` resolving to a non-stdlib declaration (step T greps that no `emptyList` is declared in
    `com.debrify.app.tv` or imported by name);
  - a missing declared type.

### 7. Coroutines, handlers, tokens, Flutter, teardown

**Coroutine.** Each `launchAddonSubtitleFetch` does `host.subtitleScope.launch { … }` on
`Dispatchers.Main + SupervisorJob()`. The body calls the suspend `StremioSubtitleService.fetchSubtitlesForAddon`
(`withContext(IO)`, a 3-attempt ladder with `delay` 500/1500 ms). The scope is **borrowed**: the activity
creates it and cancels it only in `onDestroy` (10037). The controller never cancels it.

**Tokens (owned by the controller):**
- `addonSubtitleFetchToken` is the content generation. It is bumped in `resetSubtitleState` and
  `applyManualSubtitleIdentity`, captured by `fetchStremioSubtitles` (metadata lookup) and by
  `fetchStremioSubtitlesWithImdb` (`contentToken`), and passed live by `retryAddonSubtitles`.
- `addonFetchTokens[addonId]` is the per-slot retry generation. It is incremented on every launch and
  cleared on reset.
- Guards apply after the IO result, in order: content token, then slot token.

**Flutter calls:**
- `requestMovieMetadata`, through the top-level `requestMovieMetadataFromFlutter`. There is no watchdog;
  the reply is checked against the content token.
- `searchSubtitleCatalogs` with argument map `{"query": query}`:
  - success, error and notImplemented post via `activity.runOnUiThread`;
  - a null channel or a thrown exception calls `onError` **synchronously**;
  - consumer guards are `dialog.isShowing` (dialog) and `unifiedMenu?.isVisible` (UM).

**No owned Handler, Runnable or timer.** The controller borrows `externalSubtitleHandler` only indirectly,
through phase-4 code.

**Teardown (unchanged order, `onDestroy`):**
1. `subtitleScope.cancel()` (retained);
2. `subtitleSourcesController.stremioSubtitles.clear()` (patched in place, not folded);
3. `stremioSubtitleService = null` (retained).

### 9. Hazards (each a step-T fixture or negative)

1. **Bidirectional Host coupling with the phase-4 controller.**
   - Owner → `host.subtitleController.` (18): its forwarder is computed (`subtitleController` is
     constructed earlier).
   - Phase-4 → 9 re-pointed forwarders.
   - Negatives: a snapshotting forwarder for `subtitleController`, `subtitleScope`, `playerPreferences`
     (lateinit) or `stremioSubtitleService`.
2. **Fieldless dialogs collaborator.** It is constructed eagerly at the owner slot.
   - Negatives: a dialogs field; the dialogs file reading the Host for owner state; reading `sources`/Host
     during construction.
3. **Missed `sources.`/`dialogs.` qualification** compiled against a same-name Host member (phase-11 style
   negative).
4. **Object-expression super-constructor `this`** (6220). It is classified as the activity. Positive plus a
   misclassification negative.
5. **Excluded `this.adapter`** (5973) and the **6 non-substitution pins** (`context` ×4, `getItem`, named
   argument `resources =`). Negatives substitute each one.
6. **Labels:** 10 label sites are never rewritten, including the 2 retained ones whose call becomes
   `.dialogs.`-qualified.
7. **Two braced retained-template patches** (2176, 8797). Negative: the unbraced form.
8. **New classifier form** `emptyList()` plus reuse of `-1`. A complete set of 20 proofs.
9. **Lateinit / volatile.** `playerPreferences` is `lateinit` (computed forwarder). There is no
   `@Volatile` in the unit.
10. **`onDestroy`:** 1 in-place statement between two retained statements. Negative: folding or reordering.
11. **Lint opt-in parity.** The owner carries a class-level `@OptIn(UnstableApi::class)`, a pinned
    structural span. The `lintDebug` issue set must stay identical (the dialogs file needs no opt-in).
12. **Ordering inside `resetSubtitleState`** is preserved verbatim:
    1. phase-4 `stopExternalSubtitleRendering`;
    2. clears;
    3. `subtitleTrackReadiness.onMediaReplacement()`;
    4. selector rebuild;
    5. token bump;
    6. `SubtitleSettings.resetSyncOffset()`;
    7. `offsetRenderersFactory?.setOffsetUs(0L)`.

### 11. Step T / step 0 needs

**Step 0 prerequisite (from phase 13):** `TvPlayerOriginalAccess.kt` owner-route split, done as phase
13's first step-T item. Phase 14 adds 7+ routes to that fixture, not to the helper.

**Step T:**
- the `emptyList()` classifier form plus negatives (reuse `-1`);
- the phase-14 production extraction fixture:
  - owner plus an eager fieldless dialogs collaborator, its construction pinned;
  - 20 proofs;
  - 10 cross-qualifications;
  - 4 re-point rows (14 tokens);
  - 24 patches, including the 2 braced templates and the 2 `.dialogs.` prefixes;
  - the in-place `onDestroy` patch;
- negatives: §9, plus a dialogs field, a label rewrite, and substitution of a `context`/`getItem`/named
  `resources =` site;
- compiled audit: 22 receiver sites (including the object-expression super-constructor argument), 3
  inherited `runOnUiThread` pins, 1 excluded receiver, 6 non-substitution pins;
- per-phase dispatcher keeping all historical suites;
- earlier destinations, **including `TvSubtitleController.kt`**, frozen at the phase-13 merge;
- R8/DEX mapping covering both classes, the Host, the activity Host object and the renamed anonymous
  classes.

**Step 0** characterizes the original, mostly from zero. Each prerequisite is demonstrated on the original
first; a failed prerequisite defers that slice and triggers a design re-review.

**Prerequisites:**
1. **Latch-controlled addon fetch.**
   - Use a Robolectric shadow of `StremioSubtitleService.attemptFetch(StremioAddon, String)`, the private,
     blocking per-attempt HTTP call (`TvPhase4Response` latch pattern). This keeps production
     `withContext(IO)`, the retry ladder and Main publication. Prove the IO thread and Main publication.
   - Seed addons through the profile-scoped `stremio_addons_v1` preference (`getSubtitleAddons`), or a
     shadow of it.
   - Failure paths run the real ladder with ≈ 2 s of `delay`. Throw on all 3 attempts.
   - `StremioSubtitleService` is final and constructed by the activity, so it cannot be subclassed.
   - `mockwebserver` 4.12.0 is available as a fallback.
2. **Fake Flutter channel** (the phase-2 recording messenger), for `searchSubtitleCatalogs` and
   `requestMovieMetadata`:
   - paired inline and queued main-looper replies;
   - error, notImplemented and encoded-null;
   - a null channel and a throwing `send`, both with synchronous `onError`.
3. **Dialog harness.**
   - Robolectric `ShadowDialog.getLatestDialog()` / `ShadowAlertDialog`;
   - views found in the custom container;
   - IME `IME_ACTION_SEARCH`/`DONE` and `KEYCODE_ENTER` `ACTION_UP`;
   - `ListView.performItemClick`;
   - the positive button whose listener is installed in `OnShowListener` (the dialog must be shown);
   - `ShadowToast`.
4. **Clock control** for `System.currentTimeMillis()` in `getCurrentSubtitleSearchItem` (`updatedAt`), or
   assertions that do not depend on it.

**Behaviours:**
- **`fetchStremioSubtitles` routing matrix:**
  - a custom-series id without a manual id returns early;
  - injected captions are seeded with suppression, unless a manual id is set;
  - a merged `audioUrl` clears;
  - series id, or empty → clear;
  - manual identity (series/movie item copies);
  - movie `perItemImdbIds` hit and cached-null;
  - single-item fallback;
  - Flutter metadata lookup with cache write, null result, and **stale content token**.
- **Fan-out:**
  - LOADING slots, the discovery flag and `isLoading`;
  - per-slot token versus content token (a retry during in-flight; a content switch or manual identity
    during in-flight);
  - the side-renderable filter;
  - `rebuildFlat` dedupe and URL re-pin;
  - a FAILED slot with an error, then retry;
  - the "No online subtitles" toast, only with a manual identity, and only when the last slot finishes
    empty;
  - UM versus panel refresh surfaces;
  - `clearStremioLoadingState`.
- **`tryAutoSelectAddonSubtitle` wiring:**
  - readiness × READY;
  - default/`off`/null preference;
  - forced-only and only-foreign-audio preferences;
  - manual / suppressed / addon-selected inputs;
  - `failedSubtitleUrls` exclusion, the pt-BR label match, the null-preference trailing eligible indices;
  - every branch: Off (stop plus selector disable, only if not already disabled), Wait/Keep/Addon,
    Embedded (override only if not selected), AddonTrack (index by URL + `loadStremioSubtitle`);
  - `getSubtitleSourcePriority(activity)`.
- **`resetSubtitleState`:** all fields, the selector-disable triad, the sync-offset reset order, and through
  each caller (direct VOD, PikPak, Stremio TV, IPTV navigator/Start Over Hosts).
- **`applyManualSubtitleIdentity`:**
  - no item → toast;
  - series without season/episode → prompt;
  - token bump, field values and label, stop rendering, selector disabled, panel refresh, toast text;
  - fetch with the copied item.
- **`currentSubtitleIdentityLabel`:** all 3 branches.
- **`getCurrentSubtitleSearchItem`:** payload, IPTV entry, media-item title/URL fallback, and null.
- **Search dialog:**
  - initial query, empty query, loading state;
  - 0, 1 and N results with focus/selection;
  - error, and a reply after dismiss being ignored;
  - item click for movie, series-resolved and series→prompt;
  - no current item → toast;
  - IME search / Enter;
  - `OnShowListener` focus.
- **Season/episode prompt:** default precedence (item → manual → 1), validation toast, IME Done, positive
  button.
- **Adapter rows:** text, styling, a recycled `convertView`.
- **UM column:**
  - col2 rows and badges (… / count / ⚠);
  - the tag routing to phase-4 builders;
  - col3 `SEARCH` versus `ROWS` with a pending series;
  - the identity header and `previewVisible`.
- **Addon rows:** loading, failed + retry + error `take(48)`, OK empty, and selection requiring both URL and
  addon match.
- **Search rows:** pending adjust bounds 1..99 / 1..999; fetch clears pending and hides; status rows.
- **`umPickSearchResult`:** series resolved/unresolved (`coerceAtLeast(1)` defaults, render versus hide) and
  movie.
- **`onSearchSubmit`:** state and visibility guards; `searchInitialQuery`.
- **`onDestroy`:**
  - statement order;
  - **destroy during an addon fetch** (§12.2) and a late metadata reply after destroy (§12.1), pinned as-is.

**Mutation proofs.** Apply the phase-11 lesson from the start. The unit has **67 `if`, 5 `when`, 48
`return`, 34 `?:` and 51 `?.`** sites. Build the PSI per-function coverage matrix and run a statement-level
sweep in step 0, before Claude's first independent sample. Then:
- the first sample must kill ≥ 75 %; otherwise sweep and take a second sample;
- 0b closes the gaps;
- a new JVM baseline follows.

### 12. Follow-ups found while mapping (pin as-is; do not fix)

1. **`addonSubtitleFetchToken` is not bumped in `onDestroy`.** A `requestMovieMetadata` reply that arrives
   after destroy passes the token check and runs `fetchStremioSubtitlesWithImdb`. That:
   - sets LOADING slots and `isLoading`;
   - refreshes the UI;
   - calls `launch` on the cancelled scope, which is a no-op.
2. **`launchAddonSubtitleFetch` catches `Exception`.** That includes the `CancellationException` raised when
   `onDestroy` cancels `subtitleScope` during `withContext(IO)`. The coroutine then continues: it marks the
   slot FAILED, auto-selects, can toast and refreshes the UI after destroy. Characterize it; do not fix.
3. **Catalog search has no request generation.** In both the dialog and UM paths, an older reply can
   overwrite newer results. Replies post via `runOnUiThread` even after destroy (guarded only by
   `dialog.isShowing` / `unifiedMenu?.isVisible`). A null channel or an exception calls `onError`
   synchronously, while other outcomes are asynchronous.
4. **`stremioSubtitleService` is assigned twice:** in `onCreate` 2188 and `initIptvMode` 8077.
5. **`subtitleTrackReadiness` and `stremioSubtitleService` remain shared activity state.** Move the first
   with playback start (phase 18) if wanted.
6. **Existing follow-up.** `showSubtitleTrackDialog` and `hideSubtitleSettingsPanel` (phase-4 file) still
   have no callers. Unchanged.

## Phase 14 Step 0 — original `82b16832c`

All three prerequisites were demonstrated first on the detached original, then retained in the final **172/172 passing tests** (10 concrete classes, 13 new test/fixture files). Three narrowly equivalent nodes (SDK-28 probes plus archived Android bytecode):

- `o244`, circular ProgressBar `isIndeterminate`: already indeterminate-only; the framework ignores repeating true or setting false in that state.

- `o215`, query `setSingleLine`: the immediately following non-multiline `TYPE_CLASS_TEXT` assignment reapplies single-line layout/transformation before publication. Deletion and false variants retain the asserted maxLines and IME behavior.

### Pinned quirks and follow-ups

- **Corrected late-metadata outcome:** after destroy, the reply still writes the captured per-item cache and passes the unchanged content token. The service has already been nulled, so it obtains zero addons, clears slots, marks discovery ready, sets loading **false** and launches no jobs. This supersedes Phase-14 inventory §12.1's LOADING description.
- A fetch already running when the borrowed scope is cancelled catches cancellation as an exception, publishes FAILED, retries automatic selection and can toast after destroy.
- Catalog search retains its original lack of query generations: an older visible-menu reply can overwrite newer results; hidden-menu/dismissed-dialog replies are ignored by their existing visibility guards.
- Existing user-visible English strings, filter behavior and source-policy quirks are characterized unchanged. No bug, localization or resource-lifetime fix is included.

## Phase 14 Step 0b — original boundary sweep

Claude's 17-mutation sample killed 14. The exact r03/r16 survivors now assertion-fail against all **186** phase-14 tests. Added **14 boundary tests**, all passing on the original and each with a named assertion mutation proof. A recording shadow intercepts the public suspend service call and forwards directly to its real implementation, preserving the original IO/retry/Main ladder; it observes both season/episode arguments, which a URL-only check cannot distinguish when just one number leaks. Movie fanout/retry/manual-identity calls drop both numbers; series keeps its manual/item fallback and nulls. Empty manual IDs retain normal fetch, injected-caption and embedded-selection behavior; retry's explicit empty ID/type retain their original null-only fallback semantics. Empty labels and the last-empty-addon toast are pinned separately.

The sweep runs **16 original mutations: 15 assertion kills, one equivalent**. The equivalent is **r17**: both `en` and `eng` are members of the English set and reverse-map to canonical `en`. Direct equality with either tag is also true through variant membership for the other target. Every subsequent normalization, variant, canonical and prefix branch uses the same English set/canonical prefix; the special pt-BR check is false for both. Those matching calls and that pt-BR test are the only uses of targetLanguage in the moved code. A compiled original LanguageMapper check compares **13,417 tags** (all configured variants/suffixes/case forms plus deterministic unknown tags); every result agrees. The exact r17 rerun passes all 186 characterizations. No kill is credited. Raw definitions/patches/logs/XML, immutable fixtures and source/class hashes are in `p14/step0b/`; `language-equivalence.json` records the reasoning.

### 1. Summary and recommendation

**Phase 15 = "controls I + display/audio": the dock *builder* side, not the dock *runtime* side.** One
owner + one nested collaborator for the dock, plus one sibling for display/audio settings:

- **`TvControlsDockController.kt`** (owner; 448 member lines → **≈ 560**): OTT skin install, caption,
  track height, `setupControls` (binding, click routing, focus treatments), the `DockSkinSpec` data class
  (nested → top-level `internal`), the 17 **dock-only** views it binds, and the `USE_UNIFIED_MENU`
  companion constant (file-private). Activity property `controlsDockController` at the `iptvPrevButton`
  slot (212). `@OptIn(UnstableApi::class)` at class level.
- **`TvLiveDockStyler.kt`** (nested, eagerly constructed by the owner; 260 → **≈ 290**): IPTV live dock
  setup/styling/arrangement/restore (`setupIptvControls` … `restoreCinemaIptvControlStyle`) and the two
  capture maps `cinemaIconTints`/`cinemaButtonTypefaces`. Reaches the dock views as `dock.x` (48
  compile-checked cross-qualifications), shares the owner's Host.
- **`TvPlaybackDisplayController.kt`** (sibling; 363 → **≈ 420**): aspect/resize, speed, night mode
  (`LoudnessEnhancer`), system audio-effect session, content display-match mode (`TvDisplayModeController`),
  `decoderAnalyticsListener`, `loadPlayerDefaults`, the label/value tables, the aspect/night button-label
  updaters, and the UM **display** and **audio** sections (`umDisplayModel`, `umAudioModel`, `umAudioTracks`,
  `umAudioSelectedIndex`, `showAudioTrackDialog`) plus the `DECODER_LOG_TAG` constant. Activity property
  `displayController` at the `displayMatchMode` slot (289). `@OptIn(UnstableApi::class)`.

**Phase 16 = "controls II"**: the dock *runtime* — show/hide/auto-hide timers (`controlsHandler`,
`hideControlsRunnable`), focus probes, play/pause, legacy seekbar + cinema scrub + `seekbarHandler` ticker,
title/OTT identity + extras + dock tags, loading overlay (`setResolvingState`), Next overlay,
`isCleanPlaybackState`, and the shared presentation views that phase 15 leaves activity-owned (§1.2).

### 1.1 Why this split (15/16) — measured alternatives

Group sizes (member lines incl. attached comments) and cross references (refs / distinct names):

| group | lines | refs into it from C1 (dock+styler) | refs from it into C1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| SH (show/hide/auto-hide, play/pause, focus probe, pause label) | 249 | **30 / 5** | 2 / 2 |
| SK (seekbar legacy, cinema scrub, ticker) + CS (5 cinema fields) + SV (8 seekbar views) | 485 | 6 / 5 | 2 / 1 |

| DI (display/audio, incl. UM audio+display) | 363 | 6 / 6 | 9 / 4 |

| option | phase 15 | phase 16 | temporary patches in phase 15 | other costs | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A\*** (selected) | C1 + 17 dock-only views + DI (1,071) | SH+SK+CS+SV+TI + shared views (≈ 1,110) | **3** | dock Host 58 (24 view forwarders, re-pointed in 16); 41 reflective sites / 9 routes | best ratio |
| A0 | C1 + DI, all views stay | same | 3 | dock Host **≈ 75** (41 view setters); only 3 reflective sites | rejects narrow-Host objection |
| A′ | C1 + **all** 41 C1-bound views + DI | same | **≈ 80** (SH 11, SK 33, TI 29, +7 calls) | Host ≈ 35 | too many temporary patches |
| B | SH+SK+CS+SV + DI (1,097) | C1 + TI + views (≈ 1,104) | **≈ 44** (C1 41 + TI 2) | 23 permanent `dispatchKeyEvent` patches + ≈ 30 reflective (`controlsMenuVisible` ×23) pulled forward; Host ≈ 50 | reverse dependency direction |
| D | C1 + SH + views (1,062) | SK+TI+DI (1,089) | ≈ 82 (SK 38, TI 33, DI 11) | — | worst |

A\* keeps the dependency direction the deps report recommended (C1 → SH/SK is 36 refs, SH/SK → C1 is 4):
moving C1 first costs **10 Host forwarders** (SH 5, SK 3, CS 2) and **3 temporary patches**, all consumed
by phase 16. DI rides with C1 because C1↔DI is 15 refs both ways and DI shares no state with SH/SK/TI.

### 1.2 View-ownership decision (the deps report's open question)

`setupControls`/`installOttControlsSkin` **bind** 41 view fields; their *runtime readers* differ:
- **17 dock-only views** — read only by dock/styler/display, 3 iptv controller Hosts, and 2 retained
  sites → **move to the dock owner** (single writer and its natural owner): `iptvPrevButton`,

  `ottSourcesButton`.
- **24 shared presentation views/state** — read at runtime by SH/SK/TI (phase 16) → **stay activity-owned
  in phase 15** behind computed Host `var`s (dock writes them once while binding); phase 16 decides their
  final owner (re-pointing these 24 forwarders in one whole-property row): `controlsOverlay`,

- **Session-fixed lazies stay** (guideStyle/guideTokens precedent, phases 6/12): `controlsSkin` (read by

  form, keeps `getControlsSkin` reflection on the activity, and removes one temporary SH patch. Only the
  `DockSkinSpec` *type* leaves the activity (the Host must name it).
- **Shared infrastructure stays**: `nativeAudioRouting` (the same instance is handed to

  thread), `trackSelector`, `player`, `playerPreferences`, `skipSegmentsEnabled`/`skipSegmentProviderId`

**Step-T classifier additions** (narrow, each with negatives):
1. **Typed empty `HashMap`**: `HashMap<T, U>()` with explicit type arguments and no arguments (sibling of
   the phase-11 `java.util.ArrayDeque<Int>()` form). Reject `HashMap(other)`, `HashMap<…>(16)`,
   `hashMapOf(x to y)`.
2. **Literal `arrayOf`**: every element is an int/float literal, a template-free string literal, or one
   of the allow-listed `AspectRatioFrameLayout.RESIZE_MODE_{FIT,FILL,ZOOM}` Java `static final int`
   constants. **Bytecode proof**: the display controller's `<init>` contains no `GETSTATIC` on
   `AspectRatioFrameLayout` (the constants are inlined), so no Media3 UI class initialisation moves earlier.
   Reject a call, property read, template string or non-allow-listed qualified name as an element.
3. **Reviewed anonymous object**: exactly `object : AnalyticsListener { … }` whose body has no `init`
   block and whose only property initializer is `inputFormat: Format? = null`; the object captures the
   controller only. Reject an `init` block, a state-reading property initializer, or another supertype.

### 7. Timers, handlers, native resources, teardown

- **No owned Handler, coroutine, `MethodChannel` or token.** No `progressHandler` use (the zap banner's
  progressHandler tokens are untouched).
- **Controls auto-hide** stays activity-owned until phase 16: the unit calls
  `scheduleHideControlsMenu` (9 click/focus sites → `controlsHandler.postDelayed(hideControlsRunnable,
  4 s)` when playing) and `cancelScheduledHideControlsMenu` (pause click) through Host forwarders.
- **Seekbar ticker**: `setupControls` calls `startSeekbarProgressUpdates()` (100 ms `seekbarHandler`
  loop, SK) and `setupCinemaProgressBar()` (focus/key listeners) through the Host; ordering inside
  `setupControls` unchanged.
- **View animations** (uncancelled, pinned as-is): caption fade 120 ms; classic focus scale 200 ms; OTT
  scale/lift 120 ms; no listener/animator is cleared on destroy (existing).
- **`LoudnessEnhancer` (native, owned by display):** created in `initializeLoudnessEnhancer` from
  `playbackListener` READY (1641–1642, only when null and night > 0), `onAudioSessionIdChanged`
  (2011–2013, release-then-init), `decoderAnalyticsListener.onAudioTrackInitialized` (301) and
  `applyNightMode` (when not reprepare-restarting); released by `releaseLoudnessEnhancer` on non-repeat
  media-item transition (2004), session change, route change in `applyPlaybackSpeed`/`applyNightMode`, and
  **`onDestroy` 8837** — after the three handler clears (8833–8835) and before
  `AudioEffectSession.closeCurrent(this)` (stays in the activity) and the player release. **Not** released
  in `onStop`/`onPause` (pinned as-is).
- **System audio-effect session**: `syncAudioEffectSession` → `AudioEffectSession.open(activity, id)`
  (READY 1649, session change 2009, track init); close stays in `onDestroy`.
- **`NativeAudioRouting`** (activity-owned, borrowed): `update`/`setPlaybackSpeed`/`reprepare` from the
  display controller; `reprepareIfPending` stays in `playbackListener` (1522, patched for its arguments);
  `setupPlayer` keeps passing the same instance to `NativeAudioRenderersFactory`.
- **`TvDisplayModeController`**: (re)created by `loadPlayerDefaults` (after `clear()` of a previous one),
  fed by `decoderAnalyticsListener.onVideoInputFormatChanged`, cleared + nulled at `onDestroy` 8728–8729
  (2nd/3rd statements, right after `cancelPendingIptvCatchupRequest`).
- **Analytics callbacks** run on the application (main) looper; no moved field is read off-main; no
  `@Volatile` field moves (`ottShowName`, the only volatile control field, is TI/phase 16).
- **Teardown order unchanged**: the 3 `onDestroy` statements stay in place as single-reference patches
  (phase-9 rule; not folded). `onStop`, `onPause`, `onStart`, `onResume`, `finish` untouched. Existing
  bytecode teardown helpers (`TvPhase9BytecodeAccess`, `TvPlaylistBytecodeAccess`) filter other owners and
  are unaffected; the phase-5/7/8 handler cleanup lists name only retained handlers.

### 9. Hazards (each a step-T fixture or negative)

1. Two sibling controllers at different slots + a **field-bearing nested styler** at the dock's effective
   slot (2 HashMap proofs). Negatives: omitted proof for the styler's first field; styler/display reading
   the Host or owner during construction; lazily constructed styler/display.
2. The **3 new classifier forms** (§3) incl. the `AspectRatioFrameLayout` constant-inlining bytecode proof.
3. **24 shared view/state forwarders written by the dock** (`host.x = …`): computed `get`/`set` only.
   Negative: an initialized/snapshotting forwarder (would read a `lateinit`/null at slot 212).
4. **23 `findViewById<T>` inference sites** through Host-typed targets (CHECKCAST pins; a negative with a
   widened Host type).
5. **48 styler→dock `dock.` qualifications** — compile-checked (no same-name Host member exists for the 17
   owned views); negative: a dock view accidentally added to the Host.
6. **`nativeAudioRouting` identity**: borrowed through a computed getter; negative: a forwarder that
   allocates/snapshots a routing instance (would silently desync `requiresPcm` from the renderer).
7. **`LoudnessEnhancer` release ordering**: route-change `releaseLoudnessEnhancer()` before
   `nativeAudioRouting.reprepare`/`setPlaybackSpeed`; `onDestroy` position; transition-repeat early return.
8. **Last-set-wins focus listeners** in `setupControls` (classic animation → `extendTimerOnFocus` → OTT
   re-apply list): statement order frozen; characterization per skin.
9. **`this@AndroidTvTorrentPlayerActivity` inside `pauseButton?.apply {}`** → `activity` (declared label
   substitution); negative: rewriting it to bare `this`.
10. **3 braced host templates** in the `loadPlayerDefaults` log (negative: unbraced `$host.x`).
11. **Leading trivia travels with its child**: the "UNIFIED MENU · backing" banner (7527–7532) moves with
    `umAudioTracks`; `// Aspect ratio`, `// Playback speed`, `// Night mode …`, `// ── Display`, `// ── Audio`
    move with theirs. Pin explicitly; the remaining UM backing (`subtitleSearch*` fields onward, phase 14)
    starts without the banner.
12. **Companion constants** `USE_UNIFIED_MENU` (with KDoc) and `DECODER_LOG_TAG` → file-private consts;
    the companion is a split container (partition children; `PAYLOAD_KEY` and others retained in order).
13. **`DockSkinSpec` type move** (nested private → top-level internal; retained `dockSkinSpec` lazy
    token-identical); the Host's `dockSkinSpec` getter keeps lazy first-access timing.
14. **Overloads:** `Toast.makeText` CharSequence overload ×4, `AlertDialog.Builder(Context)` ×2,
    `ContextCompat.getColorStateList(Context,int)` ×3, `LayoutInflater.from(Context)`,
    `LiveRecordingService` static `(Context)` ×2, `AudioEffectSession.open(Context,int)`,
    `TvDisplayModeController(Activity, …)` constructor — compiled descriptor audit (14 sites + 3 getters).
15. **Lint:** the dock-skin layouts stay referenced from the activity (`dockSkinSpec` keeps the
    `R.layout.view_debrify_tv_*_controls` references), but the inflation moves
    (`LayoutInflater.from(activity)`); check the phase-13 Overdraw "inferred theme" correspondence for any

  `extendTimerOnFocus` in the classic pass.
- Classic focus scale never fires (overwritten by `extendTimerOnFocus`; the code comment admits it).
- `resizeModeIndex` field default is 1 (Fill, per its comment) but `loadPlayerDefaults` defaults to 0
  (Fit); only the exception path keeps 1.
- `updateIptvControlPresentation` resets `cinemaSeekWasPlaying` on a live transition, so a scrub
  interrupted by a live switch does not resume playback.
- `LoudnessEnhancer` survives `onStop` (released only on destroy/transition/route change).
- `showAudioTrackDialog`/`showNightModeDialog` are reachable only when `unified_menu_root` is absent
  (`USE_UNIFIED_MENU` is a constant `true`).
- `cinemaIconTints`/`cinemaButtonTypefaces` capture once per button and are never cleared (hold View
  references for the activity lifetime).

Loudness and animation-cancellation shadows are observation/failure seams only. Existing tests and assertions are unchanged.

Each count below was checked by hand against the source. Terms as in phases 11–15: **patch** = token edit in
a retained activity declaration; **re-point** = edited forwarder target in an existing controller property's
Host object (that property becomes a whole-property `patched` row); **substitution** = declared edit inside a
moved body.

### 1. Summary and recommendation

**Phase 16 = "controls II": the dock runtime.** One owner with two eagerly constructed, field-bearing nested
collaborators, one shared Host, one activity property:

- **`TvControlsOverlayController.kt`** (owner; 21 members / 332 lines → **≈ 430**): show/hide/auto-hide
  (`controlsHandler`, `hideControlsRunnable`, `CONTROLS_AUTO_HIDE_DELAY_MS`), focus probe, play/pause and the
  pause label, subtitle lift, title reveal/hide, the loading/Next overlay (`setResolvingState`,
  `setNextOverlayBackdrop`, `show/fadeIn/hideNextOverlay`), `isCleanPlaybackState`, and the views
  `controlsOverlay`, `pauseButton`. Activity property **`controlsOverlayController`** at the
  `controlsOverlay` slot (210). `@OptIn(UnstableApi::class)` is **required** (`PlayerView.showController()`
  is `@UnstableApi` in media3-ui 1.8.0, verified with `javap`).
- **`TvDockIdentityPresenter.kt`** (nested `val identity`; 16 members / 311 lines → **≈ 330**): `updateTitle`,
  `guideTitleFor`, `updateOttIdentity`, `updateOttExtras`, `dockTagsFor`, the tag cache, `@Volatile
  ottShowName`, and 8 identity views. Constructor `(host)` only: it uses no activity receiver and no owner
  member (an unused `activity` parameter would add a Kotlin warning).
- **`TvSeekScrubController.kt`** (nested `val seek`; 43 members / 518 lines → **≈ 540**): the 100 ms progress
  ticker (`seekbarHandler`, `seekbarProgressRunnable`), cinema scrub (5 state fields + animator), the legacy
  seekbar overlay logic and quick seek (`seekBy`), and 11 cinema/time/scrub views. Constructor
  `(activity, host, controls)`.

**Risk: medium-high.** No Flutter channel, no coroutine, no async token. The risks are:
- **key routing**: 27 permanent `dispatchKeyEvent` patches (BACK/CENTER/DOWN/UP/LEFT/RIGHT matrix);
- focus and animation timing (300/250/220/160/200/150/100/80 ms) across **7 controls skins**, with skin-specific
  identity arms;
- the 100 ms ticker feeding the progress reporter's watch guards (`maxStableDurationMs`,
  `lastRealPositionMs`) and the skip-segment state every tick;
- the **dead legacy seekbar path** (`showSeekbar` has no caller), which needs reflective characterization;
- the widest re-point row so far: the phase-15 dock Host with 22 `get`/`set` pairs.

Existing coverage only toggles `controlsMenuVisible`/`seekbarVisible` reflectively, drives some IPTV keys,
and covers `isCleanPlaybackState` in Stremio TV wiring. Show/hide, scrub, title/identity and the Next overlay
have **no** characterization.

### 1.1 Why three files, nested, with this ownership

Group sizes (member lines incl. trivia) and measured cross references:

| group | members / lines | → SH | → SK/CS/SV | → TI | → 24 shared views | → title/next lateinit views |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SH (show/hide, play/pause, lift, label) | 13 / 260 | — | 0 | 1 | 11 | 18 |
| SK + CS + SV (ticker, scrub, legacy seekbar) | 38 / 511 | 3 | — | 0 | 33 | 0 (30 to lateinit seekbar views) |
| TI (title, identity, extras, tags, Next overlay, clean-state) | 14 / 364 | 1 | 1 | — | 25 | 30 |

- One file for SH + TI would be ≈ 624 + Host ≈ 730 lines, in the 501–800 review band, and mixes two
  responsibilities. Three files keep each ≤ 550.
- The Next overlay and `isCleanPlaybackState` go with the owner, not identity. They read
  `controlsMenuVisible`/`seekbarVisible`/`nextOverlay` and are reached from the Up Next, gate and Stremio
  guide Hosts as presentation state.
- **Nested, not sibling.** Seek and owner share `pauseButton`, `controlsHandler`, `controlsMenuVisible`
  and `showControlsMenu` (8 refs). The phase-11/13/15 precedent is cross-qualified nested collaborators:
  shared state has one owner and a missed qualification does not compile. A sibling seek at slot 206 would
  save one proof but needs 4 more Host forwarders, and the shared state would no longer be compile-checked.
- **Qualifier names.** The owner is referenced as **`controls`**, never `overlay`: `showControlsMenu`,
  `hideControlsMenu` and `isFocusInControlsOverlay` have `val overlay` locals (22 sites). Scanned
  collisions for `controls`, `seek` and `identity` in all 80 spans: **0**. `updateSubtitleControlsLift` also
  has a `val dock` local (4 sites); it needs no qualification because `controlsOverlay` is owner-owned.

### 1.2 View-ownership decision (the 24 shared views/state left by phase 15)

Rule: a view moves to the phase-16 file that is its **only runtime reader outside the dock**. The dock's
`findViewById` write keeps going through its frozen Host `var`, now re-pointed. A view stays when its readers
span several owners and retained code.

Measured reader/writer sets (excluding the dock's write; H = existing controller Host):

| view/state | readers | decision |
|---|---|---|
| `controlsOverlay` | SH 4, H zapBanner 1, dock 2 | **owner** |
| `pauseButton` | SH 5, SK 5, styler 4, dock 4, `dispatchKeyEvent` 1 | **owner** (seek reads `controls.pauseButton`) |
| `ottSkinInstalled` | SH 2, SK 6, TI 1, dock 4 (+ write), display 1, H sourceSwitch 1, `handleMetadataUpdate` 1, `playStremioTvPlaybackMap` 1 | **stays activity-owned** (multi-owner; writer is the frozen dock) |
| `ottQualityChips` (val array) | TI 2 (dock writes 3 elements) | **identity** (new `arrayOfNulls` form, §3; fallback: stay, −1 proof, +1 Host getter) |
| `ottIdentityTitle`, `…Subtitle`, `…Overline`, `…Badge`, `…Divider`, `ottRatingChip`, `ottMetaLine` | TI only | **identity** (7) |
| `debrifyTimeDisplay`, `debrifyTimeCurrent`, `debrifyTimeTotal`, `debrifyProgressLine`, `cinemaProgressBuffered`, `cinemaProgressBackground`, `ottScrubPreviewChip`, `ottScrubPreviewText` | SK (+ styler reads Current/Total) | **seek** (8) |
| `cinemaProgressContainer` | SK 3, styler 2, `dispatchKeyEvent` 3 | **seek** |
| `cinemaProgressThumb`, `cinemaSpeedIndicator` | SK, styler 1 each | **seek** |
| `cinemaSeekMode` | SK 8, styler write 1, `dispatchKeyEvent` 1 | **seek** |
| `cinemaSeekWasPlaying` | SK 4, styler write 1 | **seek** |

**Result: 23 move (owner 2, identity 8, seek 13), 1 stays (`ottSkinInstalled`).** All 23 phase-15 dock-Host
forwarders for them are re-pointed in one whole-property row. The phase-15 destination files stay
byte-identical.

**Activity-bound `lateinit` views stay** (phase-13 precedent: views bound by retained `bindViews` stay behind
computed Host getters):
- the 8 title views: `titleContainer`, `titleView`, `titleOttContainer`, `ottEpisodeBadge`,
  `ottEpisodeTitle`, `ottRatingContainer`, `ottRating`, `channelBadge`;
- the 4 Next-overlay views: `nextOverlay`, `nextText`, `nextSubtext`, `nextBackdrop`;

Moving them would cost:
- 18 `bindViews` patches with owner-typed `findViewById` inference;
- 7 more re-points/patches (`titleView` ×4 Hosts, `nextText`/`nextSubtext`, `showBufferingIndicatorDebounced`);
- an **unqualifiable** `::seekbarOverlay.isInitialized` in retained `onDestroy` (7792);
- 39 reflective retargets (`titleView` 15, `nextText` 5, …);
- a new `lateinit` move form.

Staying costs 18 Host getters and two activity-owned readiness getters (`::startupGateView`,
`::nextBackdrop`, both read by moved code).

**Also stays:** `dockSkinSpec`/`controlsSkin` (session-fixed lazies, phase-15 decision), `startupGateView`,
`playerView`, `subtitleControlsLift`, `seekFeedbackManager`, `pikPakReactivationIndicator`,

`var`), and `progressHandler` (not used by the unit). The companion constants `SEEK_STEP_MS` and

### 3. Owned state and initializer proofs

**One slot: `controlsOverlayController` at `controlsOverlay` (210).** This is after the retained seekbar
lateinit block (200–205) and before the phase-15 `controlsDockController` (212). Both nested collaborators map
to the owner's effective slot (phase-6/13/15 `nested_construction`). Pin their construction initializers
(`val identity = TvDockIdentityPresenter(host)` and `val seek = TvSeekScrubController(activity, host, this)`);
recommended position is after the owner's 5 fields. Nothing reads `controls`, Host or the dock during
construction. Every other moved field runs at 210 → **38 proofs** (39 fields − the slot field). Several run
**earlier**:
- the 4 owner fields after 210;
- identity 250–277;
- seek 231–282, 780–782, 1367, 1498;
- the handlers, which are now created before `progressHandler` (1365). That is inert: posting order, not
  handler creation order, sequences the shared main looper.

Seek 206/207 run **later** (210 instead of 206). They are inert constants and nothing reads them before 210.

| fields | form | kind | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| owner: `pauseButton = null`, `controlsMenuVisible = false` | literal | constant | supported |
| owner: `controlsHandler = Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())` | `Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())` | handler-allocation | supported (phase 10) |
| owner: `hideControlsRunnable = Runnable { … }` | `Runnable { … }` (SAM lambda, body reads nothing at construction) | allocation | supported |
| identity: 7 views `= null`, `dockTagsCacheKey = null`, `ottShowName = null` (`@Volatile`; KDoc stripped) | literal | constant | supported |
| identity: `dockTagsCache: List<DockFormatTags.Tag> = emptyList()` | `emptyList()` with declared type | allocation | supported (phase 14 binding check) |
| identity: **`ottQualityChips = arrayOfNulls<TextView>(3)`** | **new: `arrayOfNulls<T>(<non-negative int literal>)`** | allocation | step T |
| seek: `seekbarBackgroundWidth: Int = 0`, 11 views `= null`, `cinemaProgressTrackWidth: Int = 0`, `cinemaSeekMode = false`, `cinemaSeekWasPlaying = false`, `cinemaProgressAnimator = null`, `seekbarVisible = false`, `seekbarPosition: Long = 0`, `videoDuration: Long = 0` (trailing `//` comments stripped) | literal | constant | supported |
| seek: **`currentSeekSpeed: Float = 1.0f`**, **`cinemaLastAnimatedProgress: Float = 0f`** | **new: scalar float literal** (`[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?f`; phase 15 only validated floats as `arrayOf` elements) | constant | step T |
| seek: `seekbarHandler = Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())` | handler | handler-allocation | supported |

Totals: 38 = owner 4 + identity 11 + seek 23.

**Step-T classifier additions (narrow, each with negatives):**
1. Scalar float literal. Reject a negative or exponent form, a `Double`, a call, and a property read.
2. `arrayOfNulls<T>(N)` with explicit type argument and decimal literal `N`. Reject an expression size,
   `arrayOfNulls(3)` without a type argument, and `Array(3) { … }`.
3. `object : Runnable { override fun run() { … } }`. Extend the phase-15 reviewed-anonymous-object mechanism
   by **one allow-listed supertype**. Reject an `init` block, any property, a second supertype, and a
   constructor-time read.

No `lateinit` property moves. The only `::x.isInitialized` in moved code is
`::startupGateView` (5121) and `::nextBackdrop` (4547). Both properties stay, so both become activity-owned
`added` readiness getters (phase-3 rule), slot-anchored right after the controller property:
`private val startupGateViewReady: Boolean get() = ::startupGateView.isInitialized`,
`private val nextBackdropReady: Boolean get() = ::nextBackdrop.isInitialized`. No `by lazy` moves.
